source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #349 (branch fix/335-handle-validation at head 27416cb160da45e14845bc1a32f8fe844fe63113 — the #335 change (canonical handle operations validate handle indices against the instance table) with the Codex-review follow-ups (host-provided handles pass through on a local-index collision, two synthetic import-path identities of one provider resource are not distinguished at the boundary, host-supplied public-call arguments are registered at the call boundary, a resource.drop naming a host handle wins over a colliding local entry, and a borrow of a locally defined resource crosses the boundary as its representation rather than a handle index), merged with current main b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b (PRs #350 and #353); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45613750066 and 45613760858 against the branch and pull-request run 45612073405, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #349 (#335, canonical handle operations validate handle indices against the instance table; fifth re-baseline for this PR, after the third Codex-review follow-up commit 27416cb — a borrow of a resource defined in the validating program crosses the canonical boundary as the resource's representation, not a handle-table index, so the boundary validation exempts locally defined borrow leaves instead of trapping them as unknown indices). Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone three times (workflow_dispatch runs 45613767941, 45613778933 and 45613787203 on main at b20ed79513bbb12f6e4447158fd4028808ac129b; all three runs pass the gate against main's checked-in baseline, and the main control is byte-identical to that baseline on all 32 gated series). This PR's own delta against the main control is confined to the series of the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped file +9,792 B in each of component, wasi and wasi-threads and stripped .text +8,192 B (component) / +8,208 B (wasi, wasi-threads); in release-size, stripped file +5,984 B (component) / +6,000 B (wasi) / +6,016 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +4,560 B in each. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Against the previous (fourth) re-baseline, the step is +32 B stripped file and +32 B stripped .text in release for each of the three configurations, and −16 B stripped file in release-size component and wasi (wasi-threads and every release-size .text series unchanged); all twelve series are re-baselined to the branch measurements and every other baseline is unchanged. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the three branch samples and across the three main samples. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is the release component stripped file series at +11.42% (2,433,656 B to 2,711,648 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
